title: Power-series coordinates on a smooth augmented algebra completion
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative local ring and $C$ a smooth $B$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Let $\varepsilon:C\to B$ be a $B$-algebra homomorphism, and put $I=\ker\varepsilon$. There exist $n\geq0$ and a $B$-algebra isomorphism $e:\widehat C_I\xrightarrow{\sim} B[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] such that for every $c\in C$ the constant coefficient of $e(\iota(c))$ equals $\varepsilon(c)$, where $\iota:C\to\widehat C_I$ is the completion map. No Noetherian assumption on $B$ or $C$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05D5, Lemma 10.139.4, its explicit substitution construction and augmentation quotient; local freeness specialized to a local coefficient ring

proof.text: Let I be the augmentation kernel. The split conormal sequence identifies I/I² with the differentials of C over B tensored with B through the augmentation. Smoothness makes it finite projective. A finite projective module over a local ring is free of finite rank n. Choose basis lifts f_i in I.

The substitutions X_i ↦ f_i define a B-algebra map from the power-series ring to the I-adic completion. It is an isomorphism modulo squared augmentation ideals. Products of the basis lifts generate each I^k/I^(k+1), so induction gives surjectivity on every truncated quotient. Formal smoothness lifts the inverse at level k to the next level. This lift sends I into the variables ideal, hence annihilates I^(k+1). Its composite with substitution sends each variable to itself plus a term of degree k. Subtracting these corrections gives an inverse to the composite, hence substitution is injective as well as surjective at the next level. The inverses of the substitution maps commute with truncation, so passage to inverse limits gives the required algebra isomorphism.

Take the inverse of the substitution isomorphism as e. On the quotient by the augmentation ideals substitution is the identity of B, so constant coefficient of e on the completion image of c is ε(c). The construction allows n = 0; if C = B and the augmentation is the identity, the zero-ideal completion is B and the empty-variable power-series ring is B. No Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_augmented_completion_powerSeries (B C : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra B C] [Smooth B C] (ε : C →ₐ[B] B) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (e : AdicCompletion (RingHom.ker ε.toRingHom) C ≃ₐ[B] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) B), ∀ c : C, MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (e (algebraMap C (AdicCompletion (RingHom.ker ε.toRingHom) C) c)) = ε c
